descriptionChirho: Qal: to tread upon, step on, trample — the basic physical action of placing one's foot upon something, including treading grapes in a winepress, treading upon enemies, or walking on a path.
Qal (and Hifil): to bend or draw the bow — from the action of treading on the bow's end to string or bend it; by extension, to aim or shoot.
Qal: to march or advance — an extended sense of treading denoting purposeful forward movement or military advance.
Hifil: to cause to walk, lead, or guide — the causative sense of directing someone along a path, often used of God guiding his people.
Hifil: to cause to tread upon, to make trample — the causative sense of making someone or something tread on another, including threshing grain by trampling.
